## Clarifier — #2321 — All clear, advancing to `planning`

**Verdict: All clear — no blocking ambiguities.** The body is unusually
well-specified (measured inventory, explicit no-delete decision, ordering,
acceptance criteria, an explicit STOP-and-re-plan contract if the first atomic
commit is rejected). Nothing needs a user answer.

The Step-0 context pass did, however, surface **four measurements that
materially reshape the design** and one intent-preserving deviation the planner
must decide. Recording them here so the planner inherits them rather than
re-deriving.

---

### Context resolved from project knowledge

**1. The sibling routing task #2304 is DONE — no collision on `hub.py`.**
`#2304` (the routing half of the same 2026-08-14 file-cap incident) reached
`completed` at 2026-08-16T04:03Z, squash-merged to `main` as
`52ee7c026ab703c8d2119315e1c16c930348181a`. It generalized the #1108 overflow
fallback to dataset repos + bulk uploads (`hub._filecount_overflow_retry` now
covers `_upload` AND `_upload_folder_filtered`), typed the pointer write to the
canonical repo's own `repo_type`, and fixed the return-URL mapping. It also
documented the degradation this task's premise depends on: **while the
canonical repo is AT its cap the `OVERFLOW_POINTER.json` breadcrumb cannot be
written** (it is itself a new file), so consumers miss LOUDLY at the canonical
prefix rather than reading stale data. `#2321` may edit `hub.py` freely — no
live sibling owns it.

**2. A packer for exactly this job already exists on `main`: `scripts/issue1739_pack.py`.**
This is the single most important finding. Do NOT write a new archive format
from scratch. The tool (19.7 KB, landed 2026-07-30 as #1739 r4/r5) implements
the recipe `.claude/rules/upload-policy.md` § "Per-DIRECTORY file-count cap"
already prescribes for this exact problem, and it was built against the SAME
prefix this task must repack (`issue1739_ctxmap`, where a 115,941-file staging
tripped `HubDirFileCountError`):

- **pack** — one line per source file, `{"src": "<path relative to raw root>",
  "doc": <original JSON>}`, into `<group>.shardNN.jsonl` capped at
  `SHARD_MAX_BYTES = 9_000_000`, plus a `pack_manifest.json` beside the shards.
  Deterministic (sorted relpath order; re-pack of unchanged input is
  byte-identical), memory-bounded (streams one file at a time), idempotent (a
  per-group `(relpath, size, mtime_ns)` stat census in the manifest; a re-run
  repacks only changed groups), and content-hygienic (never logs file content).
- **unpack** (`--unpack`) — streams shards back into the per-file layout, with
  `--from-hf` staging via the canonical `hub.stage_hub_prefix`, manifest/sha
  verification, and never-overwrite-differing.
- `pack_manifest.json` is an **established repo-wide convention**, not a
  one-off: already consumed by `issue1739_upload.py`,
  `issue1739_wcrung_score.py`, `issue2220_readwrite.py`, `issue2091_pod.py`,
  and pinned by `tests/test_issue2220_judge_reduce.py` +
  `tests/test_issue2254_reduce.py`.

The 9 MB cap is load-bearing and directly serves this task: shards stay on the
**non-LFS Hub path**, which is quota-immune (the storage gate fires only on
LFS — see finding 4).

Known gaps the planner must close, none of them a reason to start over:
`_serialize_doc` handles JSON/text only (cannot carry `.npy`/`.npz`/`.pt`/
`.safetensors`); `group_files()` and `HF_RAW_PREFIX` are #1739-shaped and need
generalizing; and the tool **packs + uploads but never deletes the originals** —
the atomic add-then-remove commit (body scope item 3) is genuinely new work.

**3. Measured byte inventory of the 10 target prefixes — 411.4 GB, 97.9% of it LFS.**
Read-only scoped `list_repo_tree` walk (10 parallel workers, 197 s, 0 errors,
2026-08-16). The body's file counts are confirmed exactly (610,356 total). The
byte distribution was NOT previously known and it changes the design:

| prefix | files | GB | LFS files | LFS GB | median KB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| issue1489_ctx_aug | 30,360 | 53.56 | 29,793 | 53.41 | 1792.1 |
| issue1090_partial | 35,394 | 0.03 | 0 | 0.00 | ~0 |
| issue1739_partial | 36,601 | 31.95 | 22,162 | 27.32 | 47.0 |
| issue2224_screening | 41,759 | 98.83 | 296 | 98.14 | ~0 |
| issue1739_ctxmap | 43,905 | 206.01 | 9,849 | 203.76 | 6.8 |
| issue1434_writingstyle | 49,380 | 0.54 | 30 | 0.42 | ~0 |
| issue667_alllayer | 53,858 | 4.92 | 53,760 | 4.92 | 89.9 |
| issue1586_methodgen | 54,103 | 7.00 | 150 | 6.86 | ~0 |
| issue1090_pvdatagen | 58,392 | 3.01 | 29 | 2.82 | ~0 |
| issue1481_conpos_grid | 206,604 | 5.58 | 45 | 5.02 | ~0 |
| **TOTAL** | **610,356** | **411.43** | **116,114** | **402.66** | |

The load-bearing consequence: **file count and byte volume are almost
orthogonal here.** The count lives in tiny non-LFS JSON; the bytes live in a
few large LFS blobs (one file in `issue1739_ctxmap` is 69.9 GB alone).
Repacking only the **non-LFS** files frees **~494,200 slots for ~8.6 GB** of
transfer — 49.4% of the cap, zero new LFS, no storage-quota exposure. Naively
repacking everything would move 411 GB, blow past the RunPod ~130 GB per-pod
MooseFS quota on a single prefix, and duplicate 411 GB of storage (originals
persist in git history).

Reaching the body's `>= ~550k` acceptance bar therefore requires including at
least one **small-file LFS set**. The cheapest by far is `issue667_alllayer`
(53,760 `.npz` at ~90 KB each = 4.92 GB), which brings the total to ~547.7k;
`issue1489_ctx_aug`'s 29,793 `.npy` (1.79 MB each, 53.4 GB) would reach ~577k
at 6x the byte cost. The planner should present this as an explicit
slots-freed-vs-bytes-moved tier choice rather than a single number.

**4. HF storage is 17.30 TB against the project's 10.0 TB soft ceiling — already over.**
Live probe (`hub.check_hf_storage_headroom(force_refresh=True)`): `used_tb=17.30`,
`ceiling_tb=10.0`, `over_ceiling=True`, `basis='live-api'`, 407 repos. Two
consequences the plan must handle:

- Repacking duplicates bytes (the original LFS blobs stay in git history), so a
  tier-B (LFS) archive adds real storage on an account already over ceiling.
  Another reason to keep tier B to the cheap `issue667_alllayer` case.
- **Atomicity conflict:** `hub._resolve_lfs_upload_repo` reroutes LFS uploads
  to the private overflow repo when headroom is KNOWN-insufficient. That
  routing is default-OFF (`EPM_HF_OVERFLOW_ROUTING != "1"` short-circuits), so
  it will not fire unless armed — but if any tier-B path arms it, the archive
  lands in a DIFFERENT repo than the deletes, and a cross-repo atomic commit is
  impossible. The plan must keep the archive pinned to the data repo for tier B
  (routing unarmed) or state explicitly that tier B is text-only. A tier-A
  (<=9 MB non-LFS) design sidesteps this entirely.

**5. Reader-shim surface is larger than `hub.py`.** 1,406 direct
`hf_hub_download` / `snapshot_download` call sites exist across `scripts/` +
`src/` outside `hub.py`, versus 929 uses of the hub staging helpers. A shim
inside `hub.py` covers the helper path only. Two mitigations already exist and
should be reused rather than reinvented:

- `hub.resolve_sharded_text_paths` / `hub.stage_sharded_text` /
  `hub._parse_shard_manifest` already implement **manifest-first name
  resolution** for `<stem>.manifest.json` (the #2119 consumer contract in
  `.claude/rules/upload-policy.md`: probe the manifest FIRST, stage the full
  part set, verify sha256 per part, concatenate in manifest order; a missing
  part under an existing manifest is fail-loud, never a fallback). The
  `pack_manifest.json` shim is the natural sibling of this, not a new
  mechanism.
- Per finding 1, an unresolvable canonical path misses **loudly** (404 /
  fail-loud staging), never silently returns stale data — so an un-shimmed
  direct call site fails visibly rather than corrupting a result.

Retrofitting the 1,406 direct call sites is out of scope for this task (the
body's acceptance criterion is that the shim resolves an original path from
every repacked prefix, covered by a test). Worth filing as a follow-up.

---

### Design notes for the planner (not blocking, but decide explicitly)

**(a) Order of operations — intent-preserving deviation to weigh.** The body
prescribes `issue1489_ctx_aug` first "(30,360 files, smallest)" as the
semantics test. It is smallest by FILE COUNT but, per finding 3, the
**second-heaviest by bytes** (53.56 GB, 29,793 LFS `.npy`) — a poor choice for
the cheapest possible semantics test. `issue1090_partial` is 35,394 files at
**0.025 GB** (25 MB), **zero LFS files**, and **zero in-repo Python
consumers** — three orders of magnitude cheaper to round-trip, and it is the
crash-dump residue the body already flags as repack-eligible. The body's
*intent* (cheapest semantics test first) points at `issue1090_partial`; its
*letter* points at `issue1489_ctx_aug`. Recommend following the intent and
recording the deviation with this arithmetic. In-repo consumer counts for the
rest, for ordering: `issue1739_ctxmap` 47 files, `issue1090_pvdatagen` 16,
`issue1586_methodgen` 12, `issue667_alllayer` 11, `issue1481_conpos_grid` 10,
`issue1434_writingstyle` 9, `issue2224_screening` 6, `issue1739_partial` 2,
`issue1090_partial` 0, `issue1489_ctx_aug` 0.

**(b) "A SINGLE commit per prefix" needs the invariant reading, not the literal one.**
`issue1481_conpos_grid` has 206,604 files. A single commit carrying ~206k
delete operations is far past `hub.HUB_COMMIT_FILECOUNT_WARN` (2,000 staged
files/commit), and #1481 already demonstrated a 31,000-file / 135 MB commit
being killed after >20 minutes of Hub-side pre-processing. The **safety
invariant** the acceptance criteria actually state — "no file deleted that is
not present in the archive committed in the same commit" — is fully satisfied
by per-shard-group atomic commits, each adding shards N..M and deleting exactly
the files those shards contain. Recommend the plan adopt per-shard-group
atomicity and say so explicitly, rather than attempting one 206k-op commit.
`CommitOperationDelete(path_in_repo="prefix/", is_folder=True)` IS supported
(verified against the installed `huggingface_hub` 0.36.2) and is a single op
for a fully-archived subtree — but it must NOT be used where retained LFS files
live under the same subtree; those need per-file delete lists.

**(c) The cap-semantics question the body flags is likely net-of-deletes, but verify it first.**
The recorded rejection text is "Your git repo *would contain* 1000009 files
*after this push*, over the limit of 1000000" — post-push phrasing, i.e. the
server computes the resulting tree, so an add+delete commit that decreases the
count should pass. This is a hypothesis, not a verified fact. The body's
STOP-and-re-plan contract stands: verify it on the FIRST (cheapest) prefix
before touching anything else, and if that commit is rejected, report and
re-plan rather than reaching for deletion.

**(d) Reuse inventory for the plan.** Beyond `issue1739_pack.py`:
`hub.list_hf_files_under_path` / `list_hf_entries_under_path` (server-side
scoped enumeration — a bare full-tree `list_repo_files` on this repo times out,
#833), `hub.verify_repo_paths_uploaded` (retried exact-set verify),
`hub.retry_transient` (Retry-After-aware, wall-clock-budgeted — REQUIRED on
every new live Hub call site per `--check-live-hf-retry-routing`),
`hub.stage_hub_file` / `stage_hub_prefix` (atomic, headroom-asserting staging),
`hub.assert_hub_dir_filecounts` (the pre-network per-dir guard).

**(e) Venue.** Even the tier-A design moves ~8.6 GB and, per the standing
download carve-out (`.claude/rules/pods.md`), anything downloading more than
~10 GB runs on a POD, not the shared VM — where `/` is chronically near-full.
Tier A sits just under that line; adding `issue667_alllayer` (4.92 GB) puts the
round-trip clearly over it. The plan should size this explicitly and route the
verification round-trip to a CPU pod (`cpu-mid` / `cpu-bigmem`) rather than the
VM, with per-prefix streaming so no single staging step approaches the RunPod
~130 GB per-pod MooseFS quota.

---

**Consulted:** task #2304 (body + full event chain, merge `52ee7c026ab7`);
`src/explore_persona_space/orchestrate/hub.py` (3,531 lines — overflow routing,
sharded-text manifest resolution, staging helpers, dir-filecount guard);
`scripts/issue1739_pack.py` (pack + unpack, git log r4/r5);
`.claude/rules/upload-policy.md` (per-directory file-count cap recipe, #2119
manifest-first consumer contract, quota-403 LFS-only gate); `.claude/rules/pods.md`
(download carve-out, CPU intents); `.claude/rules/gotchas.md` (#833 scoped
listing, MooseFS quota); live HF probes (scoped tree walk of all 10 prefixes;
`check_hf_storage_headroom`); `huggingface_hub` 0.36.2 API surface
(`CommitOperationDelete.is_folder`).

Verdict summary: **3 WRONG**, **5 new facts to absorb**, **1 minor count

**The load-bearing CONFIRMATION.** A6 was verified EMPIRICALLY against the live
repo, not from docs: for a non-LFS file, `sha1(b"blob <len>\0" + bytes)` equals
the `blob_id` the Hub returns, exactly; for an LFS `.npz`, the `lfs` field is
populated by a plain scoped `recursive=True` walk with no `expand=True`, and
`lfs.sha256` matches the downloaded bytes. So the plan's "compare against the
live originals" guarantee has a real server-side anchor, and its choice of
`lfs.sha256` (not `blob_id`, which for LFS is the pointer's sha1) is correct.
Had this gone the other way, tier A's integrity story would have collapsed.

**The finding that changes behavior, not just wording:** a live session is
attached to #1739, which owns TWO of the ten target prefixes
(`issue1739_partial`, `issue1739_ctxmap`). Plan v3 must stop asserting
dormancy for those two, coordinate through a durable marker on #1739 (an
independent Happy session is not SendMessage-addressable), and re-probe
liveness immediately before those prefixes' commit phases with a
SKIP-and-defer branch instead of a mid-prefix drift abort.

**The finding that is a genuine safety gap:** HF sets a 60 s timeout on the
commit request and documents that the commit can still complete server-side
after a client-side timeout. On a plan whose commits carry DELETIONS, a blind
retry of a timed-out commit is unsafe. v3 must make probe-before-retry
mandatory.

# Fact-check findings to fold into plan v3 — task #2321

Phase 1.5 fact-check of `plans/v2.md` returned **3 WRONG items** and **5 new
facts the plan should absorb**. Fix all of them; keep everything the fact-check
CONFIRMED exactly as it stands.

---

## WRONG — must change

### W1. §8 row A15 — the container-disk fallback is impossible on `cpu-mid`

The plan says `fallback --container-disk-gb 80`. That is REFUSED pre-API
(exit 1): `router.py` registers `cpu3c-8-16` with
`max_container_disk_gb = 50`, and `pod_lifecycle` refuses any explicit request
whose effective disk exceeds the registered cap, telling you to route to
`cpu-bigmem`. (The RunPod API accept-bound is 80 per a 2026-07-04 probe, but
the recorded cap is the empirically-HONORED 50.)

Fix: the escalation lever is `--intent cpu-bigmem` (cap 240 GB), NOT a bigger
`cpu-mid` disk. Note that the projected 16.5 GB peak clears the 50 GB default
regardless, so this is a fallback-path correction, not a sizing change.

### W2. §8 row A5 — wrong hub.py citation

`hub.py` L48-49 is an unrelated checkpoint-ignore-patterns list. The >10 MB
LFS force-route comment in `hub.py` is at **L386**. The `upload-policy.md L806`
half of the citation is correct — keep it, fix or drop the hub.py half.

### W3. §8 row A9 + the §2 live-sibling line — "dormant" is not established for two prefixes

A live session is attached to **#1739** — `spawn_session.py list` shows
session `cmsg5qy1dz2yh3i0tuqadmffx`, pid 299995, state `running`, in worktree
`.claude/worktrees/issue-1739`. #1739 owns **two** of the ten target prefixes:
`issue1739_partial` AND `issue1739_ctxmap`.

Orchestrator-side probe (already done — use these facts, do not re-probe):
#1739 is at `awaiting_promotion`; its last substantive markers are
2026-08-12 (inline writeup/figure rounds) plus a 2026-08-14 watcher
stash-attribution note; its `list` progress column is EMPTY; the mapping is
inferred from the worktree (`~#1739`), not an `--auto` registration. Read: an
idle-but-alive interactive session, low write risk, NOT zero.

Fix — three concrete changes, do not just soften the wording:

1. **Stop asserting dormancy for those two prefixes.** Rewrite A9 to scope the
   dormancy claim to the 8 prefixes it holds for, and state the #1739 exception
   with the evidence above. Same for the §2 live-sibling line — its narrower
   claim (no in-flight work on `hub.py` packing / `issue1739_pack.py` code) may
   stand, but it must not imply no live writers.
2. **Add a coordination step** before the two #1739 prefixes are touched. An

## THE MUST-FIX — a real data-loss path that survives every check in v3

**Crash-resume shard-path OVERWRITE silently un-archives already-deleted
members.** The "no file deleted that is not present in the archive committed in
the same commit" guarantee holds PER COMMIT but can be undone ACROSS pack runs:

1. Any group with >4,000 members spans >=2 commit units (member cap 4,000;
   `issue1481_conpos_grid` has 206,559).
2. Unit A (`<group>.shard00.jsonl`, members 1-4,000) lands; its sources are now
   deleted from HEAD.
3. The driver dies mid-commit-phase and the pod is stopped/wiped — a case §6
   explicitly contemplates ("Pod stop/resume wipes /root staging | All resume
   state is Hub-derived").
4. Local census / `pack_manifest.json` / `units.jsonl` are gone, and the HF state
   mirror is written only "after each phase" (§3.4) — so mid-commit-phase unit
   definitions are unrecoverable.
5. The re-walk at new HEAD sees only members 4,001+ (unit A's sources are gone)
   and the census-keyed re-pack emits a FRESH `shard00.jsonl` holding only those.
6. The next unit's `CommitOperationAdd` **OVERWRITES** the landed shard00.
   Members 1-4,000 now exist nowhere at HEAD: sources deleted in step 2, archive
   replaced in step 6.

Every invariant misses it by construction: I1/I3/I4 reason only about DELETE
ops; I9's partition assert is scoped within ONE pack run; `probe_unit_state`
reads path PRESENCE not content; phase-6 `verify_repo_paths_uploaded` is an
exact-SET check that cannot see content replacement. Post-hoc detection is ~nil
(the 3-samples-per-prefix shim check would hit an overwritten member with
probability ~0), so the analyzer cannot weigh it — the fatal-alternative bar.

**Fix (mechanizable, cheap):** in the unit composer assert
`set(add_paths) ∩ {paths under <prefix>/packed/ at HEAD} == ∅` — one scoped
`list_repo_tree`, infrastructure the probe and postverify already use. A
legitimately re-issued "clean" unit passes (its shards are absent by
definition); a landed unit is skipped before compose; the overwrite class
becomes a loud abort. It is the upload-side twin of the never-overwrite-differing
property v1 already has and §2 cites approvingly. Plus a §12 fixture:
resume-after-partial-commit with a re-derived census must ABORT, not overwrite.

## The three Codex Must-Fix items

**F2 — destructive commits are not conditioned on the drift observation.** A
writer can modify a named source between `drift_check(unit)` and `create_commit`;
the commit then archives revision-R bytes while deleting NEWER bytes. Same window
when I11 observes `clean` and a timed-out request lands before the re-issue.
Codex's key argument is one I had not seen stated this sharply: git history
preserving the intermediate version *mitigates* the loss but does not satisfy
"archived in the same atomic commit" — i.e. it does not discharge the body's
absolute constraint, it only makes violating it recoverable. Fix: make
`parent_commit` pinning PRIMARY — each probe returns the observed HEAD SHA, passed
as `parent_commit` on that attempt, re-probe on parent conflict.

**Note this is the third independent arrival at the same race.** Claude
Methodology logged it as non-blocking Concern 1; Claude Alternatives logged it as
non-blocking Concern 2 with the added consequence that the shim then serves stale
revision-R bytes silently; Codex escalates it to conclusion-changing. The two
Claude lenses also SPLIT on the fix (Methodology: pinning keys on repo-GLOBAL
HEAD, so any unrelated fleet write spuriously fails a pinned commit ⇒
probe-then-refresh-pin is the workable form; Alternatives: traffic is near-zero
while the repo is at cap, so pinning is cheap). Adjudicating that fork is
explicitly part of the reconciler's brief — whether Codex's "re-probe on any
parent conflict" clause already answers Methodology's objection or leaves a
starvation risk under fleet write traffic.

**F1 — the cap probe can pass below the cap and be vacuous.** NEW, and the
sharpest of the three: commit A assumes the tree is at exactly 1,000,000, but the
procedure only "reports any drift". A concurrent deletion before A, or between the
exact-count read and B, puts B BELOW the cap — where add-one/delete-one may
succeed for reasons that say nothing about whether net-of-deletes is accepted AT
the boundary. That would falsely authorize artifact deletion on a probe that never
tested the hypothesis. Fix: require an exact post-A count at a specific HEAD H,
submit B with `parent_commit=H`, and if the count is not exactly the cap or H
moved, clean up only the probe files and STOP without recording a PASS. This
matters because the probe is the plan's designated zero-risk instrument for
settling cap semantics before anything is deleted — a vacuous PASS there
propagates into every subsequent prefix.

**F4 — one forgotten mock exposes the canonical repo to test mutations.** Also
NEW. §12's tests autospec `HfApi` per-boundary while the production call defaults
to `DEFAULT_DATASET_REPO`; omit one autospec and a test exercising the real commit
route issues real add/delete commits with ambient credentials. The §12 dry-run
test does not protect the other commit-path tests. Fix: an independent
test-process mutation interlock that refuses all canonical-repo `create_commit`
calls before network access unless an explicit production-apply permit is present,
with dependency-injected fakes for behavior tests. Load-bearing against the task
body's literal instruction "Do NOT test it by deleting real artifacts" — currently
that instruction is honored by convention per test rather than enforced once.

## F2 SURVIVES — `parent_commit` pinning becomes PRIMARY

Grounding: §3.4 phase 5 runs `drift_check(unit)` and then an unpinned
`api.create_commit(...)` with no `parent_commit` kwarg anywhere in the composer,
and §11 confirms the omission is deliberate ("considered, not adopted as the
primary mechanism … may ride along as defense in depth at implementation").

Why it is conclusion-changing rather than a widened recovery window — three
arguments, the first two of which no earlier reviewer made:

1. **It is SILENT.** The recovery copy sits at an unrecorded intermediate
   revision that no run artifact points to, and the shim then serves the stale
   archived bytes AS the file — breaking §3.7's own guarantee that missing
   originals "miss LOUDLY (404), never read stale data", with no error anywhere.
2. **The "traffic is near-zero" premise is backwards.** Claude Alternatives
   argued pinning is cheap *because* fleet traffic is near-zero while the repo is
   at cap. The reconciler inverts it correctly: the repo is at cap so all fleet
   pushes currently FAIL — and the moment the first prefix frees slots, QUEUED
   fleet writers start landing, including the live #1739 session that owns two
   target prefixes, precisely during the ~150-unit commit phase. Exposure is
   highest exactly where the plan assumed it was lowest.
3. **No invariant can close it** — I7 *is* the racing check, and the violated
   constraint is the verbatim user one the plan itself quotes in §3.5.

Minimal fix: `drift_check` / `probe_unit_state` return the HEAD SHA they verified
against; every deletion-bearing `create_commit` passes it as `parent_commit`; a
parent-conflict rejection routes to re-probe → re-pin → retry **under its own
backoff budget, distinct from the 3-attempt ambiguous-outcome budget**. That last
clause is load-bearing: without it, sustained fleet traffic converts a safety
mechanism into spurious prefix aborts, which is the one legitimate residue of the
Claude Methodology objection.

**The two lenses' apparent disagreement dissolved.** Codex's "return the observed
HEAD, pin it, re-probe on conflict" IS Claude's probe-then-refresh-pin with the pin
made mandatory. Claude's livelock objection targeted a STATIC pin to a stale
pre-commit HEAD, which Codex never proposed. The asymmetry decides severity: the
pinned failure mode is fail-loud-and-slow, the unpinned one is a silent stale
archive violating an absolute constraint.

## F1 STRUCK — a vacuous cap probe carries zero artifact risk

The defect is real as text (§3.6 "re-reads the live count immediately before
commit A and **reports** any drift" — reports, not aborts), but it cannot
authorize unsafe deletion: every real deletion rides inside an atomic add+delete
commit whose delete set derives from same-commit shards (I1), so if the cap
hypothesis is false the FIRST real unit is rejected and I2 applies — "no deletion
can have occurred (HF commits are atomic — rejection leaves the tree untouched)",
rc=21 STOP. The plan already designs exactly that fallback ("the first real repack
unit of `issue1090_partial` … IS the probe"), and Codex's own PH paragraph
concedes the rejection is atomic. Worst case is one wasted rejected commit plus a
re-plan. Folded in as a strong non-blocking recommendation: abort-or-recompute on
pre-A count drift instead of reporting, and pin B on the post-A HEAD, so the
probe's evidentiary value is guaranteed rather than probabilistic.

## F4 STRUCK — requires imagining a future test-authoring omission

§12's tests are injected autospec fakes and §3.4 does hardcode
`repo_id=DEFAULT_DATASET_REPO`, but the Must-Fix presupposes a defect in tests not
yet written, not one in the plan. Even under the omission there is no plausible
path to real ARTIFACT loss: fixture-derived delete sets name fixture paths, and a
delete of an absent path is rejected atomically (the same semantics the plan
already relies on); stray adds are junk-file pollution, currently cap-rejected.
The plan also already carries a dedicated zero-mutation safety test
(`test_dry_run_thread_issues_zero_mutations`). Codex's interlock — refuse
canonical-repo `create_commit` before network access absent an explicit apply
permit, e.g. an `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` conftest default — is cheap and good, adopted
as a recommendation. Worth noting it is the same instinct behind the task body's
"Do NOT test it by deleting real artifacts": turning a per-test convention into a
single enforced boundary.

That marker recorded, as the Claude Alternatives lens's MEASURED result: "no
concrete silent-wrong-result consumer was found among the 10 prefixes' readers"
(86 referencing files, 24 using listing/snapshot calls, sampled consumers all
failing loud by the repo's empty-selection convention). Codex's Must-Fix J
asserted that claim is false and named two files with line ranges. **I verified
both myself by reading the code — Codex is right, and the Claude finding is
wrong.** Recording this because the earlier marker is now a misleading durable
record, and because it is the concrete reason the plan's §3.7 residual disposition
must change.

**Consumer 1 — `scripts/issue1090_fu3_yield_replay.py` (prefix
`issue1090_pvdatagen`, 58,363 non-LFS files, tier A, IN SCOPE).** Verified at
L66-72: `paths` comes from a recursive `list_repo_tree` of the prefix; L73 derives
`cells` ONLY from paths ending `/datagen/judge_raw_pos.json`. Post-repack those
originals are gone ⇒ `cells == []` ⇒ the per-cell loop never runs ⇒ `rows == []`
⇒ the `if rows:` summary block at L119 is skipped ⇒ **`return 0`**. The program
exits SUCCESS, prints nothing about the vanished data, and emits no diagnostic.
Textbook false-green.

**Consumer 2 — `scripts/issue1481_cjk_audit.py` (prefix `issue1481_conpos_grid`,
206,559 non-LFS files, tier A, the LARGEST in-scope prefix).** Verified at L86-93:
`_download_pools` lists `{PREFIX}/raw_completions/{panel,base_arms}` and keeps

`[i1481-cjk] scan: 0/0 intruded over 0 pools`. This is worse than Codex
characterized it: not merely a silent zero in memory, but a PERSISTED false

Why the Claude lens missed them despite measuring the right population: its sample

`issue1739_natpv.py:382`, `issue1090_fu4.py:1571`) and it generalized from the

**Consequence for the plan (this is a scope change, not a wording fix).** §3.7's

## The other three Codex Alternatives Must-Fix

**D — presence can impersonate landing.** `unit_landed` accepts shard-path
PRESENCE with no content check; deterministic packing + census-keying only prove
equality while codec code and inputs are unchanged, so after a code fix or a stale
prior run the same paths may hold different bytes, and the driver can mark the unit
landed and publish new indexes against OLD shards. Converges with Claude
Alternatives' non-blocking Concern 3 (compare each landed shard's `blob_id`
against the local git-blob sha1) — Codex escalates it to blocking. Note the two
lenses found opposite halves of one missing check: Claude's Must-Fix 1 is a landed
shard being OVERWRITTEN, Codex's D is a landed shard being FALSELY TRUSTED. One
content-equality assert closes both.

**E — pod-loss resume lacks reconstructible unit identity.** Per-unit records are
local `O_APPEND` only, while state mirrors to HF "after each phase"; if the pod
dies mid-commit-phase, completed units have deleted sources and remote shards but
no durable manifest/index or unit journal, so a fresh walk cannot recreate the
original census and may omit already-landed members and publish an INCOMPLETE
index while appearing successfully resumed. Same root cause as Claude's Must-Fix 1
(local-only unit state + per-phase-only mirroring), different consequence. Codex's
fix — persist a self-identifying per-unit journal INSIDE each atomic data commit —
is strictly stronger than Claude's proposed composer assert and would close
Claude's Must-Fix 1 as a side effect. Prefer Codex's form and keep Claude's assert
as the cheap belt-and-braces.

**G — the index-availability gap is planned, not a crash window.** Data commits
delete originals before the final per-prefix `INDEX.json` commit, but resolution
STARTS at `packed/INDEX.json` — so helper-path consumers cannot resolve
already-deleted members throughout the ENTIRE commit phase. Codex sizes it for
`issue1481`: ~52 units ⇒ ≥~17 min from pacing alone, potentially hours at the
5-minute ramp threshold, and indefinite if a crash or a rejected manifest commit
intervenes. This sharpens Claude Methodology's Concern 5, which called the same
window "transient and acceptable" — it is neither transient nor bounded. Fix:
every deletion-bearing commit also publishes the index information needed to
resolve that unit atomically (or the plan explicitly withdraws continuous
availability, quiesces consumers, and ships a tested recovery SLA).

**Metadata-anchor extension: WARRANTED**, on a mechanism that is not the obvious
one. Corrupt landed metadata can never SERVE wrong bytes — each shard line carries
its member sha256 and `stage_packed_file` sha256-verifies after decode, so a wrong
offset fails loud. The damage is different: with originals deleted, an unparseable
or truncated landed `INDEX.json` makes the shim re-raise the ORIGINAL error, so
every archived original under that prefix reads as a 404 **indistinguishable from
"never existed"** — the false-absence class that invites wasteful regeneration. A
wrong group index bricks a whole group's canonical read path while phase 6 reports
success, and the live shim check samples only 3 originals/prefix, so unsampled
corruption survives acceptance. Cost asymmetry decides it: pre-cleanup it is the
same loop over the same walk (metadata are non-LFS JSON under `packed/`, local
copies still on disk, `blob_id` already returned); post-cleanup, repair means
re-downloading and rescanning every shard.

## Three findings from this reconciliation that changed the revision brief

1. **The stale-parent abort criterion must be NARROW — the Codex remedy as written
   was too aggressive.** Codex said treat a stale-parent rejection as "a clean
   drift abort". That would spuriously abort HEALTHY prefixes across the whole back
   half of the run, because unrelated fleet commits between drift-check and commit
   are the run's own expected steady state once it starts freeing slots. Correct:
   re-run `drift_check` at the new HEAD, re-issue with the new pin (bounded
   attempts), and abort the prefix ONLY when the re-check finds actual census drift
   in the unit's own source dirs.
2. **"At cap ⇒ no concurrent writes" is wrong even before any slots free.** The
   file-count cap blocks ADDS, not MODIFICATIONS — a content-replacing commit
   leaves the count unchanged and is accepted at cap. So concurrent modification of
   a named source is live from the FIRST unit onward, not merely after the run
   frees headroom. This is now the strongest single reason the `parent_commit` pin
   cannot stay optional, and it retires the "traffic is near-zero while at cap"
   premise entirely.
3. **§11's slots-per-GB figures mix denominators — presentational only.** A's
   "≈55k/GB" reproduces only on the download denominator (upload basis: 53.1k), B's
   "≈8k" only on upload (download basis: 10.8k). On ANY single consistent basis the
   A>B>C ordering holds with ≥5× gaps, so no ranking or recommendation moves — but
   relabel each figure with its basis, since it feeds the user-facing tier-C option
   at the approval gate.

must tolerate pre-existing non-v2 entries — otherwise a prefix #1739 already

- **Stage 2** — additionally refresh the manifest's shard sha256 to match the tampered bytes: **caught** at `scripts/issue2321_repack.py:687-693` — `AbortPrefix: I5 verify receipt ... STALE (manifest_sha256 mismatch)`, `create_commit` calls = 0.
